title: Edge dependence and singletons: met together at threshold level (R-028), never at the manuscript's level; in a glyph-chain procedure singletons trade against glyph predictability, not edge MI
statement: Two generators on the record, measured the same way: each text laid onto the whole book (cut book) and read on the 34 public practice evaluation pages, with the record's own statistics: F-005 (mutual information between a word's last glyph and the next word's first glyph, paragraph text), F-014 (share of word types occurring once) and F-013 (glyph entropy given the two before, bound 2.1 bits). Manuscript: 0.230, 0.711, 1.940. mtx-light's text (R-028, which on the hidden pages reproduced both F-005 and F-014): 0.170, 0.687, 2.033. My text (R-042, 23/24 on the hidden pages, F-014 the one fact missed): 0.180, 0.609, 2.092. A sweep of one setting of the R-042 procedure (seed 4, everything else fixed: the rate of words the scribe devises from an order-2 glyph chain until it gives a shape not in his tables): rate 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.25 gives singleton share 0.593, 0.634, 0.665, 0.673, 0.684, glyph entropy 2.041, 2.103, 2.150, 2.183, 2.261, and edge MI 0.177, 0.161, 0.168, 0.146, 0.169 (no trend beyond seed noise). Answer to the open question. Yes at the level of the facts' thresholds: R-028 meets edge dependence (>= 0.15) and singletons (>= 0.667) together on the hidden pages. No at the manuscript's own level: neither procedure comes near 0.23 edge MI while holding 0.71 singletons, both fall about 0.05 to 0.06 bits short. And for this family of procedures the binding trade-off is not edge dependence against singletons but singletons against glyph predictability: adding new word shapes from a glyph chain buys singletons at about 1.7 bits of entropy per unit of singleton share, crossing F-014's 0.667 only where F-013's 2.1 bound is already broken. R-028 escapes it with stock lists of locally frequent, globally rare forms rather than chain-made shapes. Limits: practice pages only; one seed per setting; F-005's statistic is the record's plug-in MI, not the shuffle-corrected value K-001 reports (fleet-opus's filing gives corrected values for other texts).
check: Rerun vs/redteam.fact_attack for F-005, F-013 and F-014 on the R-028 and R-042 texts (practice split, cut book); regenerate the sweep with more seeds and check that singleton share and glyph entropy rise together while edge MI does not move.
